title: East-West Center Graduate Degree Fellowship 2026–2027: Apply for Graduate Study at the University of Hawai‘i
summary: The East-West Center Graduate Degree Fellowship 2026–2027 is now accepting applications from eligible students seeking to pursue graduate-level study at the University of Hawai‘i at Mānoa in the United States. The fellowship is offered by the East-West Center (EWC) and is designed to support graduate study in academic fields that are relevant to the goals and objectives of the East-West Center. The fellowship is awarded through an international competition , giving eligible applicants from the United States and selected countries across the Pacific, Southeast Asia, South Asia and East Asia an opportunity to compete for graduate study support. For prospective applicants, this is an important opportunity to combine advanced academic study at the University of Hawai‘i with the broader educational, cultural and international community associated with the East-West Center. The application deadline is December 1, 2026 . East-West Center Graduate Degree Fellowship 2026–2027 at a Glance Opportunity: East-West Center Graduate Degree Fellowship Academic year: 2026–2027 Host institution: University of Hawai‘i at Mānoa Host country: United States Study level: Graduate Selection method: International competition Opening period: August 2026 Application deadline: December 1, 2026 University admission deadline for new UH Mānoa applicants: December 1, 2026 Supporting documents deadline: January 10, following the application deadline Eligible applicants: Citizens or permanent residents of the specified eligible countries and territories Academic requirement: Four-year bachelor’s degree or equivalent General GPA requirement: Minimum 3.0 on a 4.0 scale, or equivalent Study location: University of Hawai‘i at Mānoa Application contact: scholarships@eastwestcenter.org What Is the East-West Center Graduate Degree Fellowship? The East-West Center Graduate Degree Fellowship is a graduate education opportunity supporting students undertaking advanced study at the University of Hawai‘i at Mānoa . The fellowship focuses on graduate study in fields that are relevant to the objectives and mission of the East-West Center. Successful applicants therefore have the opportunity not only to pursue graduate education but also to become part of an international academic environment bringing together students and professionals connected to the United States and the Asia-Pacific region. The fellowship is awarded annually through an international competitive process. Applicants should therefore expect their academic background, qualifications and overall suitability for the fellowship to be considered alongside applications from other eligible candidates. For the 2026–2027 academic year, applications are being invited during the 2026 application cycle. Why Consider the East-West Center Graduate Degree Fellowship? Graduate education in the United States can provide students with access to advanced academic training, international exposure, research opportunities and professional networks. The East-West Center fellowship is particularly significant because it connects graduate study at the University of Hawai‘i with the broader East-West Center environment. Successful fellows can therefore benefit from an academic experience situated within an institution whose work focuses on relationships and understanding among the United States and countries and peoples of the Asia-Pacific region. The opportunity may be particularly relevant to students whose academic and professional interests intersect with areas connected to the East-West Center s goals and objectives. Where Will Fellows Study? The fellowship supports graduate study at the University of Hawai‘i at Mānoa , commonly known as UH Mānoa. The University of Hawai‘i s graduate application process is separate from the East-West Center fellowship application. This means prospective applicants who are not already classified graduate students at UH Mānoa need to complete the relevant University of Hawai‘i admission process in addition to the East-West Center fellowship application. Applicants should therefore treat the two processes as connected but distinct requirements. Who Can Apply for the East-West Center Graduate Degree Fellowship? Eligibility is geographically restricted. The East-West Center states that individuals who are citizens or permanent residents of the specified countries and territories may apply. The eligible locations are divided into the following groups: 1. United States Citizens and permanent residents of the United States are eligible to apply. 2. Pacific Region Eligible Pacific locations include the following: American Samoa Australia Cook Islands Federated States of Micronesia Fiji French Polynesia Guam Kiribati Marshall Islands Nauru New Caledonia New Zealand Niue Northern Marianas Palau Papua New Guinea Samoa Solomon Islands Tokelau Tonga Tuvalu Vanuatu Wallis Futuna Islands 3. Southeast Asia Eligible Southeast Asian countries include the following: Brunei Cambodia Indonesia Laos Malaysia Myanmar Philippines Singapore Thailand Timor-Leste Vietnam 4. South Asia Eligible South Asian countries include: Afghanistan Bangladesh Bhutan India Iran Maldives Nepal Pakistan Sri Lanka 5. East Asia Eligible East Asian countries and territories include: China Hong Kong Japan Macau Mongolia North Korea South Korea Russia Taiwan Important Eligibility Note for African Applicants Applicants should carefully review the geographic eligibility requirement before investing time in the application. The eligible-country list provided by the East-West Center does not include African countries . This means applicants from countries such as Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania, Nigeria, Ghana, South Africa, Ethiopia and other African countries are not included in the eligible-country list provided for this fellowship. There is also no separate race or ethnicity-based eligibility category stated in the information provided. Eligibility is primarily determined by citizenship or permanent residency, academic qualifications and other fellowship requirements . Academic Eligibility Requirements Applicants must satisfy specific academic requirements before the fellowship begins. For graduate programs, applicants must have obtained a four-year bachelor s degree or equivalent . The degree must be from either: An accredited college or university in the United States; or A recognized institution of higher learning outside the United States. This means applicants with undergraduate qualifications obtained outside the United States can still be considered, provided their qualification is recognized as equivalent to the required four-year bachelor s degree. Minimum GPA Requirement Applicants are generally expected to have a minimum 3.0 GPA on a 4.0 scale , or an equivalent academic performance. The GPA requirement applies to: The applicant s last four semesters of undergraduate study; or The applicant s last six quarters of undergraduate study; and All post-baccalaureate academic work , where applicable. This is an important distinction because applicants should not assume that only their cumulative undergraduate GPA will be considered. Applicants who have completed postgraduate coursework should also take their post-baccalaureate academic performance into account when assessing their competitiveness. What If Your University Uses a Different Grading System? The East-West Center recognizes that universities outside the United States may use different grading systems. The stated requirement is a 3.0 GPA on a 4.0 scale or its equivalent . Therefore, applicants whose universities do not use the U.S. 4.0 GPA system should consider how their academic results correspond to the required standard and provide accurate academic documentation during the application process. Applicants should avoid independently converting grades in a way that misrepresents their academic record. Where official documentation or institutional guidance is available, applicants should follow the appropriate process. Fields of Study The East-West Center Graduate Degree Fellowship supports graduate study at the University of Hawai‘i in fields relevant to the goals and objectives of the East-West Center . This means prospective applicants should not focus only on whether a graduate program is available at UH Mānoa. They should also consider whether their intended field of study aligns with the broader purpose and objectives of the East-West Center. Applicants are encouraged to review the fellowship s official information, frequently asked questions and award details before submitting an application. How the Application Process Works The fellowship application process involves more than simply completing the East-West Center application. Applicants who are not already classified graduate students at UH Mānoa must also apply to the University of Hawai‘i for the following fall semester. Consequently, prospective applicants should plan their application in two parallel tracks: Apply for the East-West Center Graduate Degree Fellowship. Apply for admission to the appropriate University of Hawai‘i graduate program. Both processes should be planned carefully because missing a university admission requirement can affect the overall application timeline. University of Hawai‘i Admission Requirement If you are not already enrolled as a classified graduate student at UH Mānoa, you must apply to the University of Hawai‘i for the following fall semester by December 1, 2026 . The University of Hawai‘i launches its online graduate application system on August 1 each year for admission the following year. Prospective applicants should therefore begin preparing their university application well before the fellowship deadline. This is particularly important for applicants applying to graduate departments that may have additional admission requirements. Supporting Documents Deadline The East-West Center also provides an important date after the main application deadline. To ensure timely processing of the East-West Center application, supporting documents for both the University of Hawai‘i admissions office and the relevant department applications must be completed by January 10 . This requirement applies regardless of whether the particular UH departmental deadline falls after January 10. Applicants should therefore not assume that a later departmental deadline automatically gives them additional time for the East-West Center process. A good strategy is to aim to complete all required university and departmental materials before January 10. Application Forms Required The East-West Center provides specific application forms that prospective applicants should review and complete as applicable. Two important forms highlighted in the application information are the following: 1. Academic Letter of Reference Form Applicants are required to use the Academic Letter of Reference Form and accompanying instructions provided by the East-West Center. The form is available as a fillable PDF and is intended to support the academic reference component of the application. Applicants should identify an appropriate academic referee early enough to allow the referee sufficient time to prepare and submit the required documentation. 2. Civic Engagement Letter of Reference Form The application also includes a Civic Engagement Letter of Reference Form and instructions. This component highlights the importance of applicants demonstrating engagement beyond academic achievement. Prospective applicants should therefore pay close attention to the reference requirements and select referees who can provide meaningful, specific and credible information relevant to the respective areas being assessed. Start Preparing Your References Early Reference letters can become one of the most time-sensitive components of a competitive fellowship application. Applicants should avoid waiting until the final days before December 1 to approach their referees. Instead, prospective applicants should: Identify suitable academic referees early. Identify an appropriate civic engagement referee. Provide referees with sufficient information about the fellowship. Share relevant application instructions with referees. Explain the deadline clearly. Follow up professionally before the deadline. Confirm that all required reference documentation has been completed. Strong references should ideally provide evidence rather than simply confirm that an applicant is hardworking or academically capable. Application Timeline for 2026–2027 The fellowship application cycle follows several important dates. August 1, 2026 The University of Hawai‘i launches its online graduate application system for admission the following year. August 15, 2026 The East-West Center states that applications for the 2026–2027 competition open on August 15. The fellowship webpage itself lists an opening date of August 16, 2026, so applicants should rely on the live official application portal for access and submission status. December 1, 2026 This is the main application deadline . The East-West Center states that applications for the 2026–2027 competition close on December 1. Applicants who are not already classified graduate students at UH Mānoa must also apply to the University of Hawai‘i for the following fall semester by this date. January 10 Supporting documents for the University of Hawai‘i admissions office and relevant department applications should be completed by January 10 to ensure timely processing of the East-West Center application. Step-by-Step Guide to Applying Step 1: Confirm Your Geographic Eligibility Before preparing the application, confirm that you are a citizen or permanent resident of one of the countries or territories listed by the East-West Center. This should be the first screening step because applicants from countries outside the eligible geographic areas may not qualify. Step 2: Check Your Academic Qualification Confirm that you will have a four-year bachelor s degree or equivalent before the fellowship begins. The qualification should come from an accredited U.S. institution or a recognized higher education institution abroad. Step 3: Review Your Academic Performance Check your grades for the final four semesters or six quarters of undergraduate study as well as any post-baccalaureate coursework. The general minimum requirement is a 3.0 GPA on a 4.0 scale or equivalent. Step 4: Identify an Appropriate Graduate Program Research graduate programs at the University of Hawai‘i at Mānoa and identify a program that corresponds with your academic and professional objectives. Applicants should also consider whether the field is relevant to the goals and objectives of the East-West Center. Step 5: Apply to the University of Hawai‘i If you are not already a classified graduate student at UH Mānoa, submit the required graduate admission application by December 1. Do not treat the fellowship application as a substitute for university admission. Step 6: Complete the East-West Center Fellowship Application Complete the East-West Center Graduate Degree Fellowship application and provide the information and documentation requested. Applicants should carefully check every section before submitting. Step 7: Arrange Your References Complete the academic and civic engagement reference requirements using the forms and instructions provided by the East-West Center. Give referees sufficient time to complete their responsibilities. Step 8: Complete Supporting Documentation Ensure that the required supporting documents for both the University of Hawai‘i admissions process and departmental applications are completed by January 10. Step 9: Review the FAQs The East-West Center strongly encourages prospective applicants to review its Frequently Asked Questions before applying. This is an important step because applicants can use the FAQs to clarify common issues before submitting their applications. Step 10: Submit Before the Deadline The final application deadline is December 1, 2026 . Applicants should avoid submitting at the last minute because technical problems, incomplete information or missing documents could create unnecessary complications. APPLY HERE Important Documents and Application Resources Prospective applicants should consult the official East-West Center fellowship resources before beginning their application. The key resources include: East-West Center Graduate Degree Fellowship application page University of Hawai‘i graduate admissions information Academic Letter of Reference Form and instructions Civic Engagement Letter of Reference Form and instructions East-West Center Graduate Degree Fellowship FAQs East-West Center Graduate Degree Fellowship Award Details East-West Center Graduate Degree Fellowship Student Life information Applicants who are unable to access the application materials can contact the East-West Center scholarship team at scholarships@eastwestcenter.org for assistance. What Makes a Strong Applicant? Meeting the minimum eligibility requirements does not necessarily mean that an applicant will be selected. Because fellowships are awarded through an international competition, applicants should aim to present a strong overall profile. A competitive application should clearly communicate: Strong academic preparation. A clear reason for pursuing the proposed graduate degree. A coherent academic and professional trajectory. Evidence of leadership or meaningful engagement where relevant. Demonstrated civic engagement. A clear understanding of the applicant s intended field of study. A strong connection between the proposed study and the broader objectives of the East-West Center. Well-prepared references. Complete and accurate application documentation. Applicants should ensure that their application tells a consistent story rather than presenting disconnected achievements. Pro Tip for Prospective Applicants Do not wait until the December deadline to begin your application. The application involves both the East-West Center and, for applicants who are not already classified graduate students at UH Mānoa, the University of Hawai‘i graduate admission process. A strong preparation strategy is to begin with eligibility verification, identify your preferred graduate program, review the admission requirements, contact potential referees, prepare your supporting documents and then complete the fellowship application well ahead of the deadline. Applicants should also review the official FAQs and award information before submitting the final application. Key Deadlines to Remember For the 2026–2027 East-West Center Graduate Degree Fellowship competition, applicants should keep the following dates in mind: August 1, 2026: University of Hawai‘i graduate application system launches for the following year s admission. August 15, 2026: East-West Center states that the fellowship application period opens. December 1, 2026: East-West Center fellowship application deadline. December 1, 2026: Deadline for new applicants to apply to the University of Hawai‘i for the following fall semester. January 10: Supporting documents for the UH admissions office and departmental applications should be completed for timely EWC processing. Visit HERE for more information about the East-West Center Graduate Degree Fellowship 2026–2027. Where to Get Help Applicants who experience difficulties accessing the East-West Center application materials can contact the fellowship team by email. Email: scholarships@eastwestcenter.org Applicants should use the official East-West Center resources for the most current information because application requirements, university admission procedures and fellowship details can change from one application cycle to another. Final Thoughts The East-West Center Graduate Degree Fellowship 2026–2027 presents an opportunity for eligible students from the United States and selected countries and territories across the Pacific, Southeast Asia, South Asia and East Asia to pursue graduate study at the University of Hawai‘i at Mānoa. The fellowship is particularly relevant to applicants who have strong academic backgrounds and whose proposed graduate studies align with areas relevant to the East-West Center s goals and objectives. However, applicants should carefully distinguish between fellowship eligibility and university admission requirements . If you are not already a classified graduate student at UH Mānoa, you must also complete the appropriate University of Hawai‘i graduate admission process. The most important date to remember is December 1, 2026 , which is the stated deadline for the East-West Center Graduate Degree Fellowship application and the deadline for new UH Mānoa applicants to apply for the following fall semester. Supporting documentation should then be completed by January 10 to facilitate timely processing. Before applying, prospective candidates should verify their citizenship or permanent residency eligibility; confirm that they meet the bachelor s degree and GPA requirements; identify an appropriate graduate program; prepare their academic and civic engagement references; review the FAQs; and submit all required materials well before the deadline. For the official application and the latest requirements, applicants should use the East-West Center s official fellowship application resources. title: GEF SGP CSO Challenge Program: Grants of Up to $300,000 for Civil Society Organizations Leading Environmental Solutions
summary: Civil society organizations (CSOs) working on climate change, biodiversity conservation, sustainable agriculture, ecosystem restoration, low-carbon development, pollution reduction, waste management, food security, and sustainable urban development have an opportunity to access significant funding through the GEF SGP CSO Challenge Program . The program builds on the experience of the Global Environment Facility Small Grants Program (GEF SGP) and is designed to identify, recognize, and support innovative environmental solutions developed and implemented by civil society organizations and local actors. Unlike traditional small-grant approaches, the CSO Challenge Program is intended for organizations that have already demonstrated technical and organizational capacity and have a proven record of achievement and impact. Successful applicants can receive grants of up to US$300,000 to support projects lasting up to 24 months . The funding is particularly relevant to organizations seeking to take an existing environmental solution to the next level through replication, adaptation, scaling, and expanded impact . Opportunity Overview The GEF SGP CSO Challenge Program is an initiative focused on strengthening high-impact environmental action led by civil society organizations. The program recognizes that communities and CSOs are often closest to the environmental challenges affecting their regions. These organizations frequently understand local ecosystems, livelihoods, cultural contexts, and community needs better than outside institutions. However, organizations with successful ideas may lack the financial resources needed to replicate or scale those solutions. The CSO Challenge Program is intended to address this gap by providing larger grants and tailored support to organizations with demonstrated experience and promising approaches. The program s central objective is to: Identify, reward, and support high-impact innovative environmental approaches and solutions spearheaded by civil society organizations and actors. What Is the GEF SGP CSO Challenge Program? The Global Environment Facility Small Grants Program (GEF SGP) has supported community-based environmental and conservation initiatives for decades. The CSO Challenge Program builds upon that experience while introducing a funding approach aimed at organizations that are ready to move beyond individual community-level projects. Rather than primarily supporting organizations at the earliest stages of development, the program targets CSOs that already have: Relevant technical expertise. Strong organizational capacity. Experience implementing environmental initiatives. Evidence of successful results. A demonstrated record of impact. An environmental solution or approach with potential for wider application. The ability to manage a larger grant. A clear pathway toward replication, adaptation, or scaling. Through grants of up to US$300,000 , the program provides an opportunity for established CSOs to expand solutions that have already demonstrated promise. Funding Amount and Project Duration Eligible organizations can apply for grants of up to: US$300,000 Projects supported under the program can run for up to: 24 months This funding level is significantly larger than traditional small grants and is intended to help organizations transition successful approaches from individual projects into broader initiatives capable of generating greater environmental and community impact. Applicants should therefore demonstrate not simply that their project is important, but also why additional investment is necessary and how the proposed funding will contribute to measurable growth, replication, adaptation, or scaling. What Types of Projects Does the Program Fund? The CSO Challenge Program supports initiatives that can demonstrate potential for wider environmental impact. In particular, funding can support organizations seeking to: 1. Replicate Proven Models Organizations can seek funding to reproduce an environmental solution that has already demonstrated success in one community, ecosystem, location, or context. Replication may involve taking an existing model and introducing it to: New communities. New geographic areas. New ecosystems. Similar environmental contexts. Different local or national settings. The applicant should be able to demonstrate why the existing model is successful and why it has potential to work in the proposed new setting. 2. Adapt Existing Solutions Environmental solutions do not always work identically in every location. The program therefore supports efforts to adapt proven approaches to local circumstances, including differences in: Ecosystems. Climate conditions. Community needs. Local economies. Governance structures. Cultural practices. Natural-resource availability. Livelihood systems. An organization may therefore propose to modify an existing successful approach so that it becomes effective in a different local context. 3. Test Scaling Approaches The program also supports organizations seeking to determine how a promising environmental innovation can be expanded. Scaling can involve increasing the number of communities reached, expanding geographic coverage, reaching additional beneficiaries, strengthening implementation systems, or developing partnerships that allow an established solution to reach a substantially larger population. The emphasis is on moving beyond isolated success toward approaches that can generate broader and more sustainable environmental outcomes. Five Strategic Priority Areas The program welcomes applications from CSOs working in five strategic areas. 1. Community-Based Management of Threatened Ecosystems and Species This priority area focuses on empowering communities to protect, restore, and sustainably manage ecosystems and species facing environmental pressure. Potential initiatives may involve: Biodiversity conservation. Habitat restoration. Community-based conservation. Protection of threatened species. Ecosystem restoration. Sustainable natural-resource management. Community stewardship of important ecosystems. Conservation initiatives involving local communities. The program recognizes that communities can play an important role in protecting biodiversity when they have the knowledge, resources, partnerships, and incentives required to manage natural resources sustainably. 2. Sustainable Agriculture and Fisheries and Food Security The program also supports approaches that connect environmental sustainability with food production and community livelihoods. Relevant initiatives may address: Sustainable agriculture. Sustainable fisheries. Food security. Natural-resource conservation. Climate-resilient food systems. Sustainable production practices. Community-based fisheries management. Agricultural approaches that protect ecosystems. Projects should demonstrate how environmental protection can be integrated with sustainable livelihoods and food production. 3. Low-Carbon Energy Access Another priority area is expanding access to low-carbon energy while generating wider social and environmental benefits. Relevant projects may focus on innovative approaches that: Expand access to clean energy. Reduce dependence on high-carbon energy sources. Improve energy access for underserved communities. Support sustainable local development. Generate social and economic benefits alongside environmental gains. Organizations working on community-based low-carbon energy solutions may therefore find this funding area particularly relevant. 4. Chemicals and Waste Management The program supports initiatives designed to reduce pollution and strengthen environmentally responsible approaches to chemicals and waste management. Potential areas of intervention include: Waste reduction. Waste management. Pollution prevention. Community-based waste solutions. Safer management of chemicals. Circular approaches to resource use. Initiatives protecting human and environmental health. Projects should demonstrate how the proposed approach can contribute to reduced pollution and improved environmental outcomes. 5. Sustainable Urban Solutions The fifth strategic priority focuses on innovation that can make cities and urban communities more sustainable and resilient. Potential initiatives may address: Sustainable urban development. Urban environmental challenges. Climate resilience. Sustainable resource management. Urban waste. Low-carbon urban solutions. Community-based approaches to urban sustainability. Environmental innovation in cities. This area is particularly relevant to CSOs developing solutions to environmental problems associated with rapidly growing urban populations. Who Can Apply? The program is specifically designed for civil society organizations , rather than individual applicants. Applicant organizations must satisfy the eligibility requirements established by the program. Civil Society Organization Requirement An applicant must be a legally established civil society organization . The organization must have: Legal status; and A bank account held in the organization s name. This means individuals applying independently are not the primary target of this funding opportunity. Organizations should ensure that their legal registration and financial arrangements meet the program s requirements before submitting an application. Location Requirement Applicants must be based in a GEF SGP eligible recipient country . Furthermore, the initiatives being proposed for replication or scaling must also be based in eligible GEF recipient countries. The program therefore has a defined geographic eligibility framework rather than being open to organizations from every country worldwide. Eligible Countries and Regions GEF recipient countries covered by the program are organized into four broad regions: Africa — 54 countries Latin America and the Caribbean — 33 countries Eastern Europe, Caucasus and Central Asia (EECCA) — 18 countries Asia-Pacific and Oceania — 39 countries Applicants should consult the official full country list before beginning an application because eligibility is determined according to the program s designated GEF recipient-country framework. What Makes This Opportunity Different? One of the most important features of the CSO Challenge Program is its focus on organizations with demonstrated achievement and impact . The program is not simply seeking ideas that sound innovative on paper. It is designed to support organizations that can demonstrate that their approaches have already produced meaningful results and have potential for greater impact. This makes evidence especially important. A strong applicant should be able to demonstrate: What environmental problem it is addressing. What solution it has developed or implemented. Where the solution has already been implemented. What results have been achieved. Why the solution is innovative or particularly effective. What evidence demonstrates its success. Why the solution can be replicated, adapted, or scaled. What additional funding is required to achieve expansion. How the proposed project will generate measurable environmental benefits. How communities and relevant stakeholders will participate. Inclusion Is a Major Program Priority The CSO Challenge Program strongly encourages projects that meaningfully engage: Women. Youth. Indigenous Peoples. Local communities. This means applicants should consider inclusion not merely as an additional component of a project, but as part of the design and implementation of the proposed environmental solution. Organizations should demonstrate how relevant groups will participate in decision-making, implementation, knowledge generation, resource management, or other aspects of the initiative. Projects that integrate environmental impact with meaningful community participation may therefore align particularly well with the program s objectives. Program Goals The CSO Challenge Program has four major goals. Recognize Innovative Environmental Initiatives The program seeks to identify and recognize environmental approaches that demonstrate strong potential for impact. It particularly values initiatives that can be replicated or scaled beyond their original location. Strengthen Organizational Capacity and Impact Selected CSOs can receive support aimed at strengthening their ability to design, implement, and scale innovative environmental solutions. This reflects the program s broader understanding that scaling an environmental solution requires more than money alone. Organizations may also need stronger systems, technical expertise, partnerships, knowledge, and implementation capacity. Promote Peer-to-Peer Learning and Partnerships The program seeks to facilitate knowledge exchange and collaboration among: Civil society organizations. Governments. Donors. Private-sector actors. Other relevant stakeholders. Peer learning can allow organizations to learn from environmental solutions implemented in other communities and countries while also sharing their own experiences. Support Inclusive Environmental Action The program promotes environmental approaches that meaningfully include women, youth, Indigenous Peoples, and local communities. This reflects the principle that environmental solutions are more likely to generate sustainable outcomes when the people directly affected by environmental challenges are involved in developing and implementing responses. Organizations Behind the Program The initiative is supported by the Global Environment Facility (GEF) and led by the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) , in partnership with RTI International . Global Environment Facility The GEF brings together several multilateral funds working to address major global environmental challenges through integrated approaches. According to the information provided by the program, the GEF has supplied more than US$26 billion in financing and mobilized an additional US$148 billion for country-driven priority projects over more than three decades. International Union for Conservation of Nature IUCN is a major international environmental organization with government and NGO members and a global network of volunteer experts. Its work focuses on finding practical solutions to environmental and development challenges, including biodiversity conservation, ecosystem protection, and sustainable development. RTI International RTI International is an independent scientific research institute that works across multiple disciplines, including social sciences, statistics, data, laboratory sciences, engineering, and other technical fields. Its partnership with the initiative brings additional research and technical expertise to the program. Why CSOs Should Consider Applying For an established environmental organization, a grant of up to US$300,000 can provide substantial resources for expanding a proven solution. The opportunity can be particularly valuable for organizations that have already completed pilot projects and now need funding to move toward larger-scale implementation. Potential benefits include: Significant financial support for environmental initiatives. Resources for replication and scaling. Opportunities to expand successful approaches into new locations. Support for adapting solutions to new contexts. Opportunities for organizational strengthening. Increased visibility for innovative environmental work. Opportunities for peer-to-peer learning. Potential partnerships with governments, donors, and private-sector actors. Greater environmental and community impact. How Applicants Can Prepare Organizations interested in the program should begin by assessing their readiness. Step 1: Confirm Organizational Eligibility First, verify that the organization: Is a legally recognized CSO. Has a bank account in the organization s name. Is based in an eligible GEF recipient country. Meets the program s organizational requirements. Step 2: Identify the Environmental Solution Applicants should clearly define the environmental solution they want to replicate, adapt, or scale. Avoid presenting only a broad environmental problem. Instead, explain the specific approach the organization has developed and the evidence showing that it works. Step 3: Document Previous Results Evidence of previous impact is particularly important for this program. Organizations should collect relevant information such as: Previous project outcomes. Environmental indicators. Community-level results. Number of people or communities reached. Conservation achievements. Restoration results. Changes in resource use. Partnerships established. Lessons learned. Monitoring and evaluation findings. Step 4: Develop a Clear Scaling Strategy Applicants should explain what will happen if additional funding is received. For example, will the project: Reach additional communities? Expand into another region? Replicate an existing model? Adapt an approach for a new ecosystem? Increase the number of beneficiaries? Establish new partnerships? Develop a more sustainable implementation model? The scaling pathway should be realistic and supported by evidence. Step 5: Integrate Inclusion Applicants should explain how the project will meaningfully engage women, youth, Indigenous Peoples, and local communities where relevant. This could include participation in: Project design. Governance. Implementation. Monitoring. Decision-making. Knowledge sharing. Livelihood activities. Conservation activities. Step 6: Review the Official Guidelines Before preparing a final submission, organizations should carefully consult the official Guidelines for Applicants and the complete list of GEF recipient countries. The guidelines should be treated as the authoritative source for detailed application requirements. Important Considerations for Applicants Organizations should avoid assuming that environmental relevance alone guarantees eligibility. A proposal should demonstrate a strong connection between: Existing success → proven solution → proposed expansion → measurable impact Applicants should also ensure that the requested funding is appropriate for the proposed activities and project duration. Because the program prioritizes replication, adaptation, and scaling, organizations with only an undeveloped concept and no demonstrated record of implementation may not be as well aligned as organizations with proven environmental solutions. APPLY HERE Deadline Deadline: 15th September 2026 Applicants should check the official GEF SGP CSO Challenge Program website and the current application guidelines for the latest application timeline, submission window, and any applicable deadlines before preparing or submitting an application. Official Application and Further Information Applicants should consult the official program resources for the complete eligibility requirements, country list, application guidance, and submission information. Applicants should also review the official Guidelines for Applicants and the GEF Recipient Countries list before proceeding. Visit HERE to learn more about the GEF SGP CSO Challenge Program. Conclusion The GEF SGP CSO Challenge Program represents a significant funding opportunity for established civil society organizations that have already demonstrated that their environmental approaches can work and are now ready to achieve broader impact. With grants of up to US$300,000 and support for projects lasting up to 24 months , the program is designed to help organizations move beyond isolated projects and expand successful environmental solutions through replication, adaptation, and scaling. Its emphasis on biodiversity, sustainable food systems, low-carbon energy, pollution and waste management, and sustainable urban development makes the opportunity relevant to a broad range of environmental CSOs across eligible GEF recipient countries. Organizations considering this opportunity should focus on demonstrating evidence of previous impact, organizational capacity, a credible scaling strategy, environmental significance, and meaningful community inclusion . Most importantly, prospective applicants should verify their country s eligibility and carefully review the official applicant guidelines before developing their proposal. For organizations with a proven environmental solution and a clear strategy for expanding its impact, the CSO Challenge Program could provide the financial and partnership support needed to transform a successful local initiative into a much larger environmental solution. title: ACU Stipend Scholarship 2026–2027: Fully Funded Research Master’s and PhD Scholarship in Australia for Domestic and International Students
summary: The Australian Catholic University (ACU) Stipend Scholarship offers a valuable opportunity for talented researchers seeking financial support to undertake a Research Master’s or Research Doctorate degree in Australia . The scholarship is open to both domestic and international students and combines a substantial annual living stipend with a full tuition fee offset. International recipients may also receive support for overseas student health cover and relocation expenses. With applications opening twice each year , the ACU Stipend Scholarship is designed to attract candidates with strong academic backgrounds and demonstrated research potential whose proposed research aligns with ACU’s broad areas of research expertise. About the ACU Stipend Scholarship The ACU Stipend Scholarship is offered by Australian Catholic University to support candidates undertaking accredited research higher degrees. The scholarship is funded by ACU and awarded and administered according to the ACU Research Training Program Scholarship Policy . It is intended for students pursuing: Research Doctorate degrees Research Master’s degrees Applicants can propose research in areas that align with ACU s broad areas of expertise. The scholarship is competitive, meaning applicants are assessed against other candidates through a merit-based selection process . Candidates with strong academic credentials and research potential are particularly encouraged to apply. Scholarship Benefits Successful applicants receive a scholarship package designed to provide significant financial support throughout their research degree. 1. title: Fully Funded PhD in Global Talent Mobility and Europe’s Strategic Autonomy at Utrecht University: €4,051 Monthly Salary
summary: Utrecht University in the Netherlands is inviting applications for a fully funded four-year PhD position in Global Talent Mobility and Europe’s Strategic Autonomy . The opportunity is hosted by the Faculty of Geosciences , within the Department of Human Geography and Spatial Planning , and is designed for highly motivated researchers interested in innovation, international mobility, human capital, economic geography, and the future of Europe’s knowledge and innovation systems. This is a particularly attractive opportunity for prospective doctoral researchers who want to pursue an interdisciplinary research career while working with large-scale datasets and internationally recognised researchers. The successful candidate will investigate how Europe’s ambitions for technological innovation, competitiveness, resilience, and strategic autonomy are connected to the movement of highly skilled international talent, particularly people who have completed PhDs in STEM-related fields. Unlike a conventional scholarship that simply provides a study allowance, this opportunity is a paid PhD employment position . The selected candidate will be employed by Utrecht University and receive a gross monthly salary, alongside holiday pay, a year-end bonus, pension arrangements, leave benefits, and professional development opportunities. Host Institution Utrecht University Faculty Faculty of Geosciences Department Department of Human Geography and Spatial Planning Research Sections The successful candidate will be based in the Economic Geography Section of the Department of Human Geography and Spatial Planning, while working closely with the Innovation Studies Section at the Copernicus Institute of Sustainable Development . The two research groups provide an interdisciplinary environment combining economic geography, innovation studies, migration research, and related social science disciplines. PhD Research Topic Global Talent Mobility and Europe’s Strategic Autonomy The PhD project focuses on an increasingly important question: How does Europe’s ability to innovate and maintain strategic autonomy depend on the international mobility of highly skilled talent? Talent has become a critical resource for modern innovation systems. Highly educated researchers and professionals contribute to scientific discovery, technological development, entrepreneurship, and knowledge transfer. At the same time, Europe and other regions are facing major changes in the international movement of skilled workers and researchers. Geopolitical tensions, migration restrictions, national security concerns, and changing international relationships may influence where highly skilled people choose to study, work, conduct research, and build their careers. These developments could have significant consequences for global knowledge networks and innovation. The PhD project therefore seeks to understand the relationship between: Global talent mobility International migration Doctoral education Human capital Innovation Scientific research Technological development Economic geography Institutional environments Europe’s strategic autonomy International knowledge networks A particular focus will be placed on STEM PhD recipients , who are important contributors to science- and technology-based innovation. What Will the PhD Research Investigate? The project will examine how doctoral training, international mobility, and institutional environments influence where knowledge is produced and where that knowledge is eventually transformed into technological and economic value. The research will connect perspectives from economic geography and innovation studies to investigate questions surrounding the movement of global talent and the consequences of that movement for innovation systems. The successful candidate will have the opportunity to develop unique datasets and use quantitative and mixed-method research approaches. The research may involve combining several types of information, including: PhD recipient data Career information Publication records Patent data Survey data Administrative data Online data Individual mobility information Other relevant sources concerning career trajectories and preferences This makes the position particularly suitable for applicants who are interested in data-intensive academic research and interdisciplinary approaches. Main Responsibilities of the PhD Candidate The successful applicant will be expected to take an active role in designing and implementing the research project. Key responsibilities include: 1. The project provides room for the PhD researcher to develop their own academic expertise while contributing to the broader research objectives. 2. Potential sources include: Publication data Patent information Career data Administrative datasets Survey information Online data Other sources relevant to international mobility and innovation Applicants with experience handling large-scale datasets and quantitative research will therefore be particularly well positioned. 3. Writing Research Papers The successful candidate will produce academic research papers that contribute to the completion of the PhD. The research is expected to meet the academic standards required for doctoral research and contribute to scholarly discussions surrounding migration, innovation, geography, and human capital. 4. Presenting Research The PhD candidate will have opportunities to present their research at: International conferences National conferences Academic workshops Research seminars Other scholarly events This will help the candidate develop their academic profile and professional research network. 5. Completing a Doctoral Dissertation The ultimate objective is to complete a PhD dissertation within the four-year period. The position is specifically structured with the intention that the successful candidate obtains a doctorate during the appointment. 6. Contributing to Teaching The candidate will also contribute to teaching activities within the department. Applicants should therefore be interested not only in research but also in developing their teaching and academic communication skills. Who Is This PhD Position For? title: Duke University Global Health Innovation and Policy Faculty Position 2026: Associate Professor or Professor Opportunity in the United States
summary: Duke University is inviting applications for a senior faculty position in Global Health Innovation and Policy at the Duke Global Health Institute (DGHI) in Durham, North Carolina, United States. The position is being jointly conducted by the Duke Global Health Institute, Duke-Margolis Institute for Health Policy, and Duke Global Health Innovation Center . Duke is seeking an experienced professional with significant expertise in global health innovation, health policy, health financing, or closely related areas to strengthen research, policy and leadership activities at Duke. The successful candidate will be appointed at the Associate Professor or Professor level and will have opportunities to contribute to research, policy engagement, teaching, mentorship, partnership development, external funding, and leadership within the Duke Global Health Innovation Center and the wider university. Duke University Global Health Faculty Position: Key Details This is a senior-level academic and professional opportunity for an established global health expert with a strong record of research, external funding, publications, stakeholder engagement and leadership. The main details of the position include: Institution: Duke University Institute: Duke Global Health Institute Position title: Faculty Position in Global Health Innovation and Policy Academic level: Associate Professor or Professor Position type: Non-tenure-track faculty Location: Durham, North Carolina, United States Primary appointment: Duke Global Health Institute Track: Research or practice track Appointment: Full-time, 9- or 12-month appointment Initial appointment: Three years Reappointment: Possible at the conclusion of the initial three-year term Position ID: Duke-DGHI-FACULTY [#32464] Subject area: Global Health The position is intended for a senior individual who can combine academic excellence with practical impact in global health innovation and policy. What Is Duke Looking For? Duke is looking for a candidate with significant expertise and experience in one or more of the following areas: Global health innovation Health policy Health financing Policy analysis Operational research Research on health innovation Development and introduction of health innovations Scaling health innovations in low-resource settings Policy engagement Global health systems The institution is particularly interested in professionals who have demonstrated the ability to move beyond research alone and translate knowledge into practical solutions that can be implemented in real-world settings. Duke describes innovation broadly. It may involve something entirely new or something that has been newly adapted to a particular local context and produces meaningful impact. Such innovation could take the form of: A product A service A programme An enterprise An applied solution The university emphasizes that successful innovation should be effective, scalable, sustainable and equitable . Experience in Low-Resource and Global Settings Although the position allows flexibility regarding specific topics, populations and contexts, Duke has a particular interest in candidates who have worked on health innovation in low-resource contexts globally . Relevant experience may include leading: Research on health innovations Policy analysis Operational research Development of health innovations Introduction of health innovations Scale-up of health innovations Policy engagement activities Experience across different low-resource settings is particularly relevant because the successful candidate will be expected to understand how innovations can be adapted to different environments rather than assuming that one solution will work identically everywhere. Duke Welcomes Non-Traditional Career Paths An important feature of this opportunity is Duke s openness to candidates who have followed non-traditional professional paths. The position specifically welcomes team-science-oriented professionals who have moved between different sectors during their careers. Examples include professionals with experience across: Universities and academic institutions Government Multilateral organizations Social enterprises Implementation organizations Practitioner settings This means candidates do not necessarily need to have followed a purely academic career trajectory if they can demonstrate strong relevant expertise, leadership, research, policy and practical experience. Leadership and Management Responsibilities Duke is also seeking an individual with substantial management and leadership experience . The successful candidate could serve in a faculty leadership capacity at the Duke Global Health Innovation Center . Leadership responsibilities may include: Managing people Managing budgets Managing organizations or programmes Representing the Center externally Engaging funders Working with governments Engaging implementation partners Supporting business development Developing partnerships Advancing funded programmes Traveling domestically and internationally when necessary The position therefore goes beyond traditional teaching and research responsibilities. It is designed for a senior professional who can help build partnerships, attract resources, manage programmes and represent Duke in global health innovation activities. Research, Policy and Practical Impact One of the central features of the position is the connection between research, policy and practical implementation. The successful candidate is expected to contribute to research and policy efforts while also demonstrating an understanding of how evidence can influence real-world health systems and programmes. This makes the position particularly relevant to professionals who can demonstrate that their work has moved from academic research into areas such as: Government policy Health programme implementation Innovation scale-up Public-sector decision-making Stakeholder engagement Health financing Health-system improvement Partnerships with implementation organizations Duke is looking for someone who can understand both the academic and practical dimensions of global health innovation. External Funding Experience A significant record of extramural funding is one of the required qualifications for the position. Duke is particularly interested in applicants who have obtained funding from diverse sources, including: Governments Foundations Industry The position s long-term salary support will come predominantly from extramural grant funding, although additional internal sources may contribute over time through activities such as teaching and administrative responsibilities. Because of this funding model, competitive candidates must be able to demonstrate their ability to communicate the value of their work and develop funded programmes that are sustainable and add value to the Duke Global Health Innovation Center s portfolio. Duke Global Health Institute and Duke-Margolis will support the successful faculty member in transitioning into the institution and developing successful programmes. Teaching and Mentorship Opportunities The position also places considerable importance on teaching and mentorship . Duke is seeking an applicant who is passionate about mentoring students and developing the next generation of global health professionals alongside their research and policy activities. The successful faculty member may mentor: Undergraduate students Global Health majors Graduate students in the Master of Science in Global Health programme Graduate students in other Duke programmes Doctoral students across the university Medical school doctoral students Postdoctoral scholars Junior faculty The faculty member may also participate in students ongoing research and studies. In addition, the successful candidate could develop new courses related to: Global health systems Innovation Health policy Health financing They may also teach existing courses in these areas. Appointment Structure and Work Location This is a full-time 9- or 12-month appointment at the rank of Associate Professor or Professor. The primary appointment will be within the Duke Global Health Institute, and the position will be a regular-rank non-tenure-track appointment in either the research or practice track. The initial appointment is for three years , with eligibility for reappointment at the end of that period. Rank and salary will be determined based on the successful candidate s qualifications and experience. There is also potential for a joint appointment in another department or school at Duke University. Because the role involves extensive collaboration, teaching, mentoring and partnership responsibilities, candidates are expected to be able to work in the United States and maintain regular presence in Durham, North Carolina. Relocation or substantial on-campus engagement is expected. About the Duke Global Health Institute The Duke Global Health Institute (DGHI) was established in 2006 as a university-wide institute bringing together faculty from across Duke. Its vision is focused on achieving health equity for vulnerable populations around the world. The institute works across several areas, including: Preparing global health leaders through interdisciplinary education. Conducting research into major global health challenges. Designing policies. Developing evidence-based interventions. Partnering with international and local organizations. Supporting locally grounded and collaborative projects. Developing innovative solutions to global health challenges. The DGHI community includes staff, primary and secondary faculty, affiliate faculty and adjunct faculty. The institute also emphasizes values including humility, compassion, respect, cultural sensitivity, collaboration, diversity, inclusion and commitment to impact. Duke-Margolis brings together expertise from the Washington, DC policy community, Duke University and Duke Health. Its work focuses on important health-policy challenges and aims to improve: Health Health equity The value of health care Health policy Health-care implementation The institute combines interdisciplinary research, education and engagement to help inform policymaking and implementation. Duke Global Health Innovation Center The position is also closely connected to the Duke Global Health Innovation Center (Duke GHIC) . Duke GHIC works at the intersection of: Health innovation Health policy Global health The Center collaborates closely with its partner organization, Innovations in Healthcare , a Duke-affiliated nonprofit organization. According to the vacancy information, Innovations in Healthcare works with more than 100 healthcare innovators across more than 90 countries as well as public and private sector organizations. Together, the organizations work to: Improve access to quality healthcare. Improve affordability of healthcare. Scale promising health innovations. Study health innovations. This broader institutional environment provides an important context for understanding why Duke is seeking someone with both research expertise and practical experience in innovation and policy. Required Qualifications Applicants must meet the stated required qualifications. 1. Doctoral or Terminal Degree Candidates must hold a doctoral or terminal degree in a relevant field . Research Experience Applicants must have experience conducting either quantitative or qualitative research related to global health innovation and policy. Candidates should therefore be able to demonstrate a substantive research record connected to the subject areas of the position. 3. Experience Across Low-Resource Contexts Applicants must have experience, or a credible pathway, for translating their work across multiple low-resource contexts globally. The position specifically identifies: Low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) Low-resource settings in the United States This requirement emphasizes the importance of understanding how global health solutions can be adapted and implemented across different settings. 4. Significant Extramural Funding Record Applicants must have a significant record of extramural funding . This is an important requirement because the position s long-term salary support will rely predominantly on external grant funding. Candidates should therefore be able to demonstrate a history of successfully developing, securing or contributing to externally funded programmes. 5. Academic and Non-Academic Publications Candidates must have a record of publishing in both academic and non-academic formats. Examples listed by Duke include: Journal articles Op-eds Policy papers Open letters Blogs This demonstrates that Duke is looking for someone who can communicate research and policy ideas to both academic and broader public audiences. 6. Policymaker and Stakeholder Engagement Applicants must also have a record of engaging with policymakers and stakeholders. Relevant stakeholders may include: Government agencies Advocacy groups Public-sector organizations Private-sector organizations Other policy and implementation partners Candidates should therefore be able to demonstrate that their work has involved engagement beyond academic institutions. Preferred Qualifications In addition to the required qualifications, Duke identifies several preferred qualifications that could strengthen an applicant s profile. Experience mentoring trainees. While these are listed as preferred rather than required qualifications, applicants who possess them may be particularly well aligned with the position. What Type of Candidate Is Duke Seeking? The overall profile described in the vacancy is that of a senior global health professional who can operate across several domains. An especially strong candidate would be able to combine: Academic expertise through advanced qualifications and research. Practical experience applying global health innovation in real-world settings. Policy expertise and experience engaging policymakers. External funding success from governments, foundations, industry or other sources. Leadership experience involving people, budgets and organizations. Communication expertise demonstrated through academic and public-facing publications. Teaching and mentorship ability . International experience , particularly across low-resource contexts. Partnership-building skills with governments, funders and implementation organizations. The position is therefore intended for an established professional rather than an early-career applicant. title: European Union Press and Information Officer Job in Switzerland 2026: Salary, Requirements, Responsibilities and How to Apply
summary: The European Union Delegation to Switzerland and the Principality of Liechtenstein has announced a new employment opportunity for an experienced communications, media, public relations or international affairs professional. The position is for a Press and Information Officer (m/f/x) within the Political, Press and Information Section of the EU Delegation in Bern, Switzerland. This opportunity is particularly relevant for professionals with substantial experience in media relations, strategic communication, digital communications, public diplomacy, journalism, public relations and event management who also have strong knowledge of German, French and English. The successful applicant is expected to begin work on 1 March 2027 . Press and Information Officer Job Opportunity at the EU Delegation The European Union is an economic and political partnership made up of 27 European countries and plays an important role in international affairs through diplomacy, trade, development assistance and cooperation with global organizations. Outside the European Union, it is represented through more than 140 diplomatic representations known as EU Delegations. These Delegations perform functions comparable in some respects to embassies and represent the EU in relations with governments and other stakeholders. The EU Delegation to Switzerland and the Principality of Liechtenstein is based in Bern, Switzerland . It works closely with the embassies and consulates of the 27 EU Member States and represents the European Union in dealings with the Swiss government on matters falling within the EU s responsibilities. The advertised Press and Information Officer will become part of the Delegation s Political, Press and Information Section. The role combines press relations, public diplomacy, social media, digital communication, event management, strategic communication and a smaller policy component. Position Details The position provides an opportunity to work directly within a diplomatic environment and contribute to the communication and public diplomacy activities of the European Union in Switzerland and Liechtenstein. Key details include: Position: Press and Information Officer (m/f/x) Group: Local Agent Group I Section: Political, Press and Information Section Location: EU Delegation to Switzerland and the Principality of Liechtenstein, Bern, Switzerland Contract: Fixed-term employment contract Contract duration: Two years Renewal: Possible, subject to budgetary availability and operational considerations Probationary period: Three months Expected start date: 1 March 2027 Working arrangement: Full time Working hours: 37.5 hours per week, Monday to Friday Additional requirements: Occasional evening and weekend work and travel for work missions The successful candidate will work under the supervision and responsibility of the Head of the Political, Press and Information Section. The Press and Information Officer will have a central role in representing and communicating the activities, policies and values of the European Union in Switzerland and Liechtenstein. The successful applicant will act as the EU Delegation s spokesperson and will advise the Ambassador on communication-related matters. The position will also serve as a key point of contact between the Delegation and journalists and media organizations. The officer will contribute significantly to the Delegation s overall press, communication and visibility strategy while managing its digital presence and developing content for social media, websites and video platforms. Another major component of the position is public diplomacy. This includes organizing events, engaging stakeholders and developing outreach activities designed to strengthen awareness and understanding of the EU, its activities and its values. Main Duties and Responsibilities Approximately 85% of the position s time will be dedicated to press, communication and public diplomacy, while approximately 15% will be dedicated to policy-related work. 1. Press, Communication and Public Diplomacy The largest part of the position focuses on communication and public diplomacy. Public Relations and Media The Press and Information Officer will be responsible for: Maintaining and developing professional relationships with local and international journalists. Working with media organizations and government press agencies. Preparing and distributing press releases, press reviews and articles for publication. Preparing interviews and speeches for the Head of Delegation. Developing and implementing public diplomacy strategies designed to improve perceptions and understanding of the EU in Switzerland and Liechtenstein. Preparing speeches, briefings and other information materials for the media. Monitoring local and European media. Preparing media reports. Managing requests from journalists and coordinating responses with appropriate internal stakeholders. Organizing media coverage during official missions and events. Collaborating with EU Headquarters services and strategic communications task forces to maintain consistent messaging and communication strategies. This means the successful applicant will need to be comfortable working in a fast-paced media environment where accuracy, speed, diplomacy and strong judgment are essential. 2. Social Media and Digital Communication Digital communication is another major component of the role. The officer will lead the Delegation s digital and social media strategy and will be responsible for managing and producing content for relevant social media platforms and the Delegation s website. Responsibilities include: Developing informative, engaging and accurate digital content. Creating and implementing digital communication plans. Developing social media campaigns. Managing cross-posting activities. Supporting livestreaming and event coverage. Monitoring social media analytics and performance. Recommending improvements to strengthen digital communication. Improving the Delegation s online visibility. Coordinating digital campaigns with external service providers. Candidates therefore need more than conventional writing or journalism skills. The position requires practical understanding of modern digital communications, social media strategy, analytics, web publishing and multimedia communication. 3. Event Management and Public Outreach The successful applicant will also lead or coordinate public diplomacy and outreach activities. This includes: Preparing public diplomacy events. Organizing public outreach activities. Supporting high-level visits and site visits. Working on events involving the Ambassador and other EU officials. Coordinating with cultural, academic and diplomatic partners. Strengthening the impact of public diplomacy activities. Organizing cultural and visibility events that promote EU values and activities. This aspect of the position makes event management and stakeholder engagement important areas of expertise. 4. Strategic Support and Administration The Press and Information Officer will also: Support the preparation of reports and strategic documents. Assist with internal and external communication plans. Support planning and management of the Delegation s press and information budget. Assist with procurement and contract management. Policy Responsibilities Although the majority of the position focuses on communication and public diplomacy, approximately 15% of the officer s time will be dedicated to policy. The policy component includes monitoring, policy analysis and reporting concerning EU-Switzerland cooperation in EU programmes , including areas such as: Erasmus+ Research Innovation Science Culture Candidates who understand European affairs, EU institutions and EU-Switzerland relations may therefore have an advantage when demonstrating their suitability for the position.
